title: Detector and anti-pattern resolution report
summary: Final cleanup pass after the art-direction wave (EXP-034–037, EXP-020). All confirmed anti-patterns were redesigned or removed; false positives are documented below with rationale.

heightTransitions.description: EXP-037 detector: no height-based CSS transitions; use transform or mask instead.

findings.reason: Dead rule. The pseudo-element's height is auto-determined by `top: -1.5rem; bottom: -1.5rem;` positioning — no explicit `height` property is ever set, so the transition had no visible effect. The `--rail-revealed` CSS variable set by HudNavigation.tsx was intended to drive a height calc but the CSS consumer was never written. Removed the dead transition. If a row-reveal animation is desired in the future, it should use clip-path or mask-image (clamped at `--rail-revealed * --rail-row-pitch`).

sideStripeCallout.description: Decorative side-stripe (colored left border) callout pattern.

findings.reason: The `prose.css` comment explicitly documents the design decision: 'hairline — no colored side stripe'. The blockquote is styled with a full background panel and a plain border-top, not a colored left stripe. No CSS class named `.side-stripe`, `.callout`, or similar exists in the codebase. The anti-pattern was evaluated and rejected at design time; no change needed.

decorativeEyebrows.description: EXP-036 rule: no repeated mono-uppercase eyebrow scaffolding on routes; hierarchy through scale only.

findings.reason: The `.article-next-eyebrow` ('Next note') appears exactly once per article page, inside the `.article-next` continuation footer. It labels the 'next article' section for wayfinding — a specific UI component role. EXP-036 forbids 'repeated mono-uppercase eyebrow scaffolding' as route structure (e.g. section headers used as section-level navigation scaffolding across the page). A single functional label in a continuation component does not violate this rule. The star-marker HUD eyebrows (`star-marker-card-eyebrow`) live in the hero system and similarly serve a specific functional UI role, not structural page scaffolding.

findings.verdict: false-positive — intentionally kept dead per code comment
findings.reason: The `.hud-nav-button::before` pseudo-element is set to `content: none; display: none` as an explicit design decision (the connector tick was removed). The hover/current `::before` rules that set `width` and `background` are effectively no-ops. The code comment states: 'Kept as a display:none rule (rather than deleting) so the hover/current/active ::before rules below are harmless no-ops.' This preserves the rule structure and prevents future accidental regressions if the tick is re-enabled.

deadStyleRules.description: CSS rules with no reachable effect.

resolved.finding: Configuration hint: remove esbuild from ignoreDependencies
resolved.action: Removed `esbuild` from `ignoreDependencies` in knip.json. `esbuild` is declared in `devDependencies` and does not need to be ignored.

resolved.finding: Unlisted dependency: sharp (scripts/brighten.mjs, gen-favicons.mjs, inspect-joins.mjs, optimize-media.mjs, overlay-diff.mjs)
resolved.action: Added `sharp: "*"` to `devDependencies` in package.json. `sharp` was already listed in `pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies` (for native build scripts) but not declared as a devDependency.
Removed. These camera look-offset constants are not imported by any consumer. The actual camera offsets are set inline in the scene builder.

Removed. Superseded by the richer `resolveMotionPreference()` in `src/lib/motionPreference.ts`, which also handles the manual override. The simpler OS-only version in config.ts was no longer imported.

Removed. The comment on EXPLORATION_TRIGGER_AT already stated: 'NOTE: the HUD is now ALWAYS visible (see HeroIsland — explorationMode starts true), so nothing reads this anymore.' Both constants were dead.
Removed. These were intended for the beat opacity trapezoid calculation but sceneTable.ts uses hardcoded numeric values in each scene definition. No consumer imports them.
Removed. The `resolve()` function composed sceneTable walkers into one LifecyclePosition object but was never imported by any consumer. Also removed the now-orphaned `LifecyclePosition` interface.

Removed the re-export `STAGE_COUNT = SCROLL_SECTION_COUNT` from timeline.ts. `STAGE_COUNT` is already exported from `src/hero/scroll.ts:99`. No consumer imports `STAGE_COUNT` from timeline.ts; the canonical name used by importers is `SCROLL_SECTION_COUNT`.

Removed the `export` keyword from these three shader strings. Only `tesseractBeamFrag` is imported (by `src/pages/behind-the-build.astro` to display a code excerpt). The vert/glow shaders are no longer used since the tesseract scene was removed from the live hero; `behind-the-build.astro` only excerpts the beam fragment shader for documentation.

falsePositives.reason: Intentional dev-only page. Used by `scripts/shoot-blueprint.mjs` for visual regression tooling. Not reachable from production routing (ENG-003 verified this). Knip's entry-point analysis does not resolve Astro dev-route conventions.

All three are imported in `src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro` via `<script>` module imports (`import '../scripts/decodeHover'` etc., lines 496/499/503). Astro's `<script>` tags are bundled by Vite and their imports are resolved correctly. Knip does not analyze Astro `<script>` block imports as TypeScript entry points; the files appear unused to Knip but are live at runtime.

`scripts/shoot-blueprint.mjs` imports from `'playwright'`. The `playwright` module is provided as a direct sub-dependency of `@playwright/test` (declared in devDependencies). Since the script is a dev-only tool and the module is transitively available, this is acceptable. Declaring `playwright` separately would pin a second version and risk divergence from `@playwright/test`'s bundled version.

These are source-of-truth string literals for localStorage keys used in Astro inline scripts (`is:inline`) that cannot import TypeScript modules. The comment on HUD_STATE_STORAGE_KEY explicitly states: 'The inline script can't import this module — no bundler on an is:inline script — so it spells the SAME literal and MUST be kept in sync with this value.' Tagged `@public` in JSDoc so Knip's `['-public']` tag filter suppresses them.
